I will push for an aligned approach to promoting statehood with the Mayor, Council, the DC Delegate, and the shadow delegation.
responses.congressResponse: The White House and Congress should not be allowed to overturn our laws without fierce opposition from our Council and our residents. I will use my voice as a Councilmember to publicly voice my opposition, including speaking to local and national media outlets; consider all legal remedies; speak directly with Members of Congress; and continue to underscore to residents how critical it is for them to be involved in fighting for Statehood and protecting home rule.
responses.partners: I will work with organizations actively working for DC Statehood and protecting home rule, including Free DC and DC Vote. I will also work closely with our partners in the DC Democratic State Committee, many of whom are providing strong leadership and actively planning DC Statehood advocacy efforts.
responses.voterInvolvement: I will continuously support organizations and residents fighting for Statehood, including those like the League of Women Voters who are involved in proactive voter education. Many DC voters work on Democratic campaigns in other states; we need to ensure they know which candidates have pledged to support DC Statehood and loudly refuse to volunteer for or donate to those who have not.
responses.additionalComments: Even when Democrats controlled the White House and both Chambers of Congress, we were denied Statehood, which is proof that we have to take ownership of this fight and not wait for the Democratic party to deliver it to us. We must start planning and organizing now, lining up national partners and actively educating our Democratic allies. No elected official of any party should be able to claim our support without fully backing  DC Statehood.

responses.topThreeActions:
We are witnessing nothing short of an assault on DC's democracy and autonomy. These actions are completely unacceptable, unnecessary, costly, and unconstitutional. They represent creeping fascism that threatens not just DC residents' ability to govern ourselves, but the safety, dignity, and fundamental rights of our most vulnerable neighbors—particularly our immigrant communities who are being terrorized by ICE raids and deportations.

As an ANC1E Commissioner I voted consistently in support of Statehood and in opposition to federal overreach. That included (1) opposition to Congressional interference with 16 bills to roll back DC laws and (2) support for the swift adoption of the DC budget without Congressional interference as well as (3) resolutions affirming Sanctuary City status. On a personal note, joining Statehood actions with Free DC has been a particularly meaningful way to be in community with other Ward 1 residents.
responses.intendedActions:
The role of Councilmembers in resisting this federal overreach is not passive—it requires bold, strategic, and relentless action. As Ward 1 Councilmember, I will approach this fight on multiple fronts:
First and most importantly, I will continue standing and speaking out against Trump and federal interference at every opportunity and publicly denouncing his actions. While silence can be viewed as strategic, I see it as complicity. DC residents deserve a Councilmember who will name what we're facing: fascism, white supremacy, and authoritarian federal overreach that treats DC residents as second-class citizens without full democratic rights. I will use my platform to make clear that these actions are attacks not just on local autonomy but on the fundamental principles of democracy and self-governance. As Councilmember, I do not support our community being terrorized and will use fierce resistance and my legislative powers and organizing skills to fight back!

Second, I will use the Council's legislative powers to close loopholes in local law that allow for inappropriate cooperation with federal authorities like ICE. DC has declared itself a sanctuary city, but that commitment means nothing if local agencies and resources are being used to facilitate deportations and immigration enforcement. I will introduce or co-sponsor legislation that: explicitly prohibits DC government employees and agencies from cooperating with ICE except where absolutely required by law; prevents the use of DC resources, facilities, or personnel to support federal immigration enforcement; strengthens protections for sensitive locations like schools, hospitals, and places of worship; and creates penalties for violations of these policies. 

Third, I will use the Council's oversight and investigative powers to document federal overreach and hold hearings that expose the human cost of these attacks. I will demand that DC agencies report on every instance of federal interference: How many times has ICE requested cooperation? How are federal deployments of the National Guard affecting public safety and community trust? What is the fiscal impact of blocked budget funds on critical services? What legal violations are occurring? These hearings will serve multiple purposes: creating a public record of federal abuses, amplifying the voices of residents directly harmed, building political pressure for resistance, and identifying specific areas where local action is needed. I will invite legal experts, immigrant rights advocates, constitutional scholars, and most importantly, DC residents experiencing this persecution to testify and share their stories.

Fourth, I will advocate for dedicating DC government resources to legal challenges against unconstitutional federal actions. The Office of the Attorney General should be filing lawsuits challenging every significant federal overreach—from budget blocks to forced cooperation with immigration enforcement to violations of the Home Rule Act. I will use my budget powers to ensure the OAG has adequate resources for this litigation.  Attorney General Brian Schwalb has already filed multiple lawsuits challenging Trump administration overreach, including suits against the attempted federal takeover of MPD and the deployment of National Guard troops in the District, which he has described as an illegal "military occupation." His office has argued that these federal actions violate the Home Rule Act and represent "the gravest threat to Home Rule that the District has ever faced." As Councilmember, I will ensure that the OAG has robust budget allocations to continue and expand this critical litigation, recognizing that legal challenges are one of our most powerful tools for protecting DC autonomy. I will also use my oversight powers to publicly support AG Schwalb's efforts, amplify the cases he's bringing, and pressure the Mayor and other agencies to fully cooperate with legal strategies to resist federal overreach. The Attorney General cannot fight these battles alone—he needs the full backing of the Council, adequate resources, and coordinated action across DC government.
 
Fifth, I will work to ensure that DC government actively protects residents rather than passively allowing federal persecution. This means: creating emergency funds to support residents facing deportation or federal prosecution; ensuring that DC's identification programs remain accessible to all residents regardless of immigration status; maintaining and expanding language access so that non-English speakers can access services and know their rights; and using every available tool in local government to create barriers to federal enforcement and sanctuaries for vulnerable residents. Because Ward 1 has the highest concentration of immigrant residents in the city, I will leverage my Council position to ensure that our non-profit organizations who protect and serve our immigrant neighbors are well-resourced and represented by their elected officials. We should have their back and demonstrate that with our legislative and budgetary power and authorities!
responses.congressResponse: I will work directly with Members of Congress who support DC statehood and autonomy to build federal legislative strategies to protect our self-governance. While we cannot rely on Congress to save us—particularly under Republican control—we must maintain relationships with allies who can introduce legislation, use committee hearings to expose abuses, and build public pressure. My seven years as a registered federal lobbyist gave me experience navigating Capitol Hill, building relationships with congressional staff, and understanding how to influence federal policy even from disadvantaged positions. I will leverage these skills to advocate for DC autonomy, budget release, and legislative protections against federal overreach.
responses.partners: I will partner with legal clinics and nonprofit organizations with experience in organizing campaigns to mobilize, educate, and train DC residents to know their rights and protect themselves from lack of due process and harm. This includes: funding and promoting know-your-rights trainings, particularly for immigrant communities; supporting legal defense funds and rapid response networks that can intervene when ICE conducts raids; ensuring that DC residents understand their Fourth Amendment protections against unreasonable searches and seizures; and building community defense networks where neighbors look out for each other. My decade of community organizing through Georgia Avenue Thrive taught me that residents with knowledge and collective power can resist even well-resourced oppression. We must build infrastructure that allows our community to protect itself, not wait for government institutions to save us.
responses.voterInvolvement: As a Ward 1 resident for over 20 years and ANC Commissioner for a decade, I've walked these streets not as a policymaker observing from afar, but as a neighbor, a community organizer, and someone deeply invested in the safety and well-being of every person who calls our ward home. I co-founded and led what is now Georgia Avenue Thrive—a community led initiative evolving from a public safety taskforce that brought together residents, small businesses, and local government to address safety concerns not through increased policing, but through community activation, economic development, and collaborative problem-solving. I've seen firsthand that real community comes from investment in people and neighborhoods. DC is under attack by President Trump and Congress right now, and now is the time to come together and fight together.
responses.additionalComments:
As a candidate for DC Council in Ward 1, I am deeply alarmed by what we are witnessing — not just here in DC, but in cities across this country. We are watching democratic norms erode in real time. We are seeing the will of voters undermined, local decision-making attacked, and power consolidated in ways that silence communities instead of uplifting them.

And I’m angry.

I’m angry because the people who bear the brunt of democratic backsliding are Black and Brown residents — the very communities who have fought hardest to expand access to the ballot, to housing, to safety, to education, to opportunity. In DC, a majority-Black city with no full voting representation in Congress, our lack of statehood is not an accident. It is the result of unbalanced power rooted in structural racism — a system that has long been comfortable controlling Black political power while denying Black political self-determination.

When local decisions are overridden, when budgets are interfered with, when our autonomy is treated as conditional, it sends a clear message: our democracy is fragile, and it is not distributed equally.

We cannot separate today’s democracy crisis from white supremacy. White supremacy is not just about hate; it is about power — who holds it, who protects it, and who is denied it. Structural racism has shaped whose voices are centered and whose are dismissed. And when democracy weakens, those already pushed to the margins are the first to feel the impact.

What we are dealing with today isn’t new. It has always existed in different forms — voter suppression, disenfranchisement, redlining, over-policing, economic exclusion. What’s different is the face it wears and the boldness with which it operates at a time when we should be progressing, not moving backwards as we are today.
But history also teaches us something else: when democracy is threatened, people organize. People build. People fight forward.
It’s time to level the playing field so all people can win. It’s time to strengthen local power, protect our rights, fight for statehood and ensure that DC residents have full voice and representation.

Let’s free DC. 

Thank you for your consideration!

responses.topThreeActions:
As a prominent organizer in DC, I have had the opportunity to speak at actions and marches with thousands of DC residents marching for Statehood & DC autonomy. Whether it was the January People’s March, the September We Are All DC March, October No Kings rally, or the actions led by the Families not Feds Coalition, I believe strongly in locking arms with fellow residents to fight for autonomy. At a Families not Feds Coalition event this past January outside the Wilson Building, I called for an end to the illegal federal occupation of the District, the end to MPD collaboration with ICE, and the strengthening and enforcement of our sanctuary status. I have joined Free DC’s lobbying efforts to Congress to demand Statehood from federal officials. Actions such as these are critical in the broader movement to win Statehood. I am proud to have joined in these actions alongside organizers across DC pushing for Statehood and full DC autonomy. It is critical to bring as many of our residents together in this fight as possible, and to spread our message to elected officials across the country. 

An action I am especially proud to have taken was testifying before the DC Council about the impact of federal overreach that I have witnessed in our communities. In October, I testified at a public roundtable on human rights violations held by the Committee on Public Works and Operations. In my testimony, I spoke about my experience on the ground, protecting our residents from warrantless attacks, and how federal overreach has instilled fear in our communities. As Councilmember, I would work with my colleagues to call for additional public hearings to ensure Ward 1 constituents’ voices can be heard and acted upon by elected leaders within the Wilson Building.

I am also proud of the organizing I have done in the streets, alongside other community members, to support neighbors in getting to work and school safely in the face of ICE. I regularly support ICE watch in the northern part of Ward 1, and I volunteer with the Bancroft Safe Streets team, where I’ve seen firsthand how dangerous it is for so many of my neighbors to get to work or parents to get their kids to school. I also have volunteered to pack groceries for neighbors who are unable to leave their homes. As Councilmember, I want my office to serve as a central hub for organizing across the Ward, and will work to ensure that our networks of organizers and mutual aid are coordinated to best meet the needs of those most impacted by continued federal overreach.

I released my “Stand Up for DC” platform in September 2025 to outline what I plan to do as Ward 1 Councilmember, and have talked about Statehood and DC autonomy on various platforms several times over the course of my campaign. Achieving Statehood must be a high priority for any leader in DC, and as Councilmember I will continue to platform and spread awareness of these issues, encourage my constituents to engage in advocating for DC to finally have full right to self-govern, and work with the national organizations that have endorsed me to make DC Statehood an important issue that every federal elected must take a stance on.
responses.intendedActions:
There are two choices in a time of rising authoritarianism: collaboration or resistance. As Ward 1’s Councilmember, I will leverage my office’s power to stand up for DC autonomy, advance our fight for Statehood, and protect the people of DC from a hostile federal government. I will do this by: 


Organizing to make DC Statehood a national issue: I am grateful to have been endorsed by national organizations like Run for Something, Our Revolution, and Working Families Party, and to have relationships with Congressional Democrats from my years of organizing in the Democratic Socialists of America. DC needs leaders who know how to build, maintain, and leverage such relationships to fight for Statehood – not only here in DC, but in every single jurisdiction around the country. DC Statehood is a vital fight for our entire democracy, a core civil rights issue, and every Democrat across the US should understand what is at stake, and what could be possible should we finally have full autonomy and representation in Congress. 


Defending DC autonomy, democracy, and civil rights: From fighting back against rollbacks on District laws to protecting and expanding the rights of LGBTQ+ and immigrant residents to standing up for bodily autonomy and abortion access, I will work every day to make sure DC residents are protected from federal overreach as we organize to advance our cause of Statehood. I will also work to ensure that unhoused neighbors receive the safety and dignity they deserve, without undue cruelty from a federal force as we saw this summer. 


Investing in local structures. DC’s Office of the Attorney General has been critical in defending DC autonomy and must continue to be well-funded, well-resourced, and supported by the full weight of the District government. OAG has been under attack by Congressional Republicans, and DC Council cannot comply with these attacks by cutting resources and reducing capacity. If elected, I will consistently work to ensure OAG is properly funded and capable of using every power available to protect DC autonomy. 


Enforcing and defending the Sanctuary Values Act: DC’s own Mayor has facilitated attacks on home rule by complying in advance with the Trump agenda by attacking immigrants herself. By attempting to repeal the Sanctuary Values Act, stripping immigrants of healthcare benefits through the defunding of Alliance, and making DC a less affordable and safe city. As a Councilmember, I will fight to ensure that the Sanctuary Values Act remains intact and that there are consequences for officials who break it, and will work to fund our full social safety net – especially programs that serve residents who are most vulnerable to attacks by Republican overreach. 


Working to end DC’s and MPD’s cooperation with ICE: Through oversight and legislation, I will work to close loopholes in our Sanctuary Values Act and ensure that MPD is complying with our local laws. I am supportive of actions such as Councilmember Janeese Lewis George’s Safe Community Places and Policing Act, which would end MPD’s transportation of ICE agents in District-owned vehicles, and would seek to introduce and pass similar legislation while holding MPD accountable. 


Fighting for federal workers: With the maximum benefit for unemployment set at just $444 a week, many federal workers have not been adequately served by DC’s safety net, which is why I will fight to raise benefits and fix the unemployment insurance system. Additionally, I will work to make sure that former federal workers have a pipeline into District government agencies, so that DC gets stronger with an influx of high skilled workers into the areas we need it most. 


Organizing With and For Our Community: I will dedicate constituent services resources to bolster community organizing, especially helping kids get to school safely, supporting federal workers, and providing unhoused members with resources. I will work with the Office of Human Rights on improving and enforcing protections for vulnerable communities like immigrants, the unhoused, queer and trans folks, and others.
responses.congressResponse:
District leaders cannot be afraid to show up to Congress and lobby for our home directly. We cannot cower in the Wilson Building while Congress uses our city as a political pawn. As a Councilmember, I will be an active and outspoken advocate for DC’s right to self-govern – speaking at actions, lobbying lawmakers on the Hill, collaborating with organizers, and rallying my colleagues to do the same. For instance, in coalition with organizers fighting for DC autonomy and alongside our elected Congressional delegate, I will commit to lobbying members of Congress on District priorities on a regular basis, encouraging and leading my Council colleagues to join me on the Hill as well as our constituents.

But this fight is not one that DC should ever have to take on alone, which is why I will work to establish and maintain good relationships with Congressional Democrats to make sure they understand that this fight is theirs too – the working people of DC should never be treated as test subjects for federal governance. And the more interference we face, the more our autonomy is restricted, the clearer the fascistic plans of the Trump administration will become. DC may be first, but other blue cities and states should know that they will face the same treatment we do. 

We need elected officials here in DC to be our strongest advocates for autonomy and Statehood, and that means organizing electeds from around the country to be our surrogates in the halls of Congress. As an organizer myself, I know that the relationships we build are our strongest assets to safeguarding our future. I will bring these skills to the Wilson Building to organize my colleagues, and to the halls of Congress to fight for DC Statehood.
responses.partners:
Our Council, the Mayor, the U.S. House Delegate, and Shadow Delegation must fight as a unified bloc alongside community partners like Free DC to promote and achieve Statehood to ensure that the voices of 700,000 Washingtonians do not continue to lack representation and autonomy in the long term. 

I will prioritize working with community organizations. Specifically, I will partner closely with Free DC to promote Statehood and organize DC residents to advocate for it in the halls of Congress. I am proud to have organized alongside Free DC to demand the right to self-determination for District residents, at Free DC marches demanding an end to the federal occupation and by canvassing small businesses on the U St Corridor with the Ward 1 team to encourage them to proudly affiliate as a Local Business for a Free DC. As Councilmember, I will work with Free DC and other groups like the Families not Feds Coalition to rally community members and fellow Councilmembers to visit Capitol Hill to defend DC’s autonomy as Congress introduces legislation limiting our powers or overturning our laws. If elected, I will also work to proactively lobby members of Congress about the need for Statehood - collaborating with fellow progressives across the country to help pressure key representatives.

I also would prioritize building a close partnership with DC’s Congressional Delegation — our next Delegate to the United States House of Representatives, our two Shadow Senators, and our Shadow Representative. As an organizer, I have worked alongside our delegation on issues related to DC autonomy and look forward to working closely with our next Delegate. If elected, I will make it a priority to maintain frequent communication and collaboration with our Statehood champions in Congress to help safeguard DC from future attacks and organize support for our fight. I will coordinate with the office of our next Delegate to ensure that the voices of Ward 1 constituents in particular are represented in committee hearings, floor speeches, and introduced legislation. I will also seek to support the Delegate’s efforts in pressuring every Democrat in the U.S. House and U.S. Senate to co-sponsor the Washington, D.C., Admission Act. Given the unique roles of the Shadow Representative and Shadow Senators in lobbying for Statehood & protection of Home Rule, I will coordinate with their offices to prevent Congress from overturning local DC laws, fund DC priorities like a dedicated source of federal funding for WMATA, and promote education & awareness on DC Statehood to bring the fight for Statehood to every jurisdiction and ensure that this is an issue that is top of mind for voters around the country. Winning Statehood will require more than just a fight to defend home rule – we must win over Congressional representatives and their constituents to show that our fight is their fight as well.
responses.voterInvolvement:
As a tenant organizer and union member, I believe that building a coalition of working people will be critical in our sustained fight for Statehood — and I will work to build that organizing infrastructure alongside DC’s organizers if elected. I will also build strong relationships with tenant groups, unions, Advisory Neighborhood Commissions, faith communities, schools, and allied civic organizations to bring the fight to Statehood to residents in every block within Ward 1 — ensuring that residents are educated about why Statehood matters. My office will make clear in communications with constituents how our lack of Statehood tangibly results in harms to good governance — such as cuts to healthcare due to federal overreach into our budget — and help our constituents understand what actions they can take to push for autonomy and Statehood.

Moreover, I believe strongly that protecting constitutional rights requires a government that has earned the trust of our residents. My office will hold regular office hours, host community forums, and provide know-your-rights trainings so residents understand their protections from federal overreach and know how to report violations — whether to my office or through testimony at a Council committee hearing. Oversight should not only happen inside the Wilson Building—it’s 365 days a year anywhere at any time.
responses.additionalComments:
For 226 years, DC has lacked statehood and full voting representation, which has always and continues to disproportionately harm our Black and brown neighbors. Despite our Home Rule, Congress serves as a roadblock to our progress as a District — whether it’s blocking local funds from being spent to provide life-saving abortion services for women on Medicaid, the lack of fully legalized adult-use marijuana, or the overturning of our tax code that would defund the District’s Child Tax Credit and increase child poverty.

Statehood would allow us to better protect our home by making sure that all working people can thrive here, including immigrant families and our LGBTQ+ neighbors. It would stop the federal government from taking control of our police department and give us control over our budget, so we can serve working families. It would mean District government officials cannot be hauled in front of hostile Congressional Republicans on a whim to defend our laws. And it would finally give us representation in votes on federal policy that impact the 700,000 people who live here. 

In recent years, we have seen how federal authority can be used to undermine our local democracy. DC residents are treated as second-class citizens in our nation’s capital, despite the fact that we pay federal and local taxes. And we cannot accepts those limitations passively — we must fight for fair representation in Congress, and for a true right to self-governance. As an elected official, my role will not be to preemptively comply with federal overreach — it will be to represent residents and defend their rights to the fullest extent possible under the law.

The Council’s January 2026 report examining human rights violations shows what District residents already know: our local agencies must be more accountable to our local government, more transparent to our residents, and work to protect the civil rights of our residents. For the good of the District, we must implement the recommendations made in this report, and as Councilmember doing so will be one of my top priorities. I can’t stress enough that the Council must hold our agencies accountable to our locally decided laws. In a time of rising facism, that act in itself is resistance.
 
I will also actively defend the District against federal interference — both in the Wilson Building and in our communities. When Congress or federal agencies attempt to override local laws or pressure the District into cooperating with policies that harm residents, local leaders must push back. That means defending and expanding sanctuary protections, ending agency contracts and executive orders that carry out unlawful surveillance, and making sure District agencies follow the law. And it means showing up in our neighborhoods, alongside community organizers, faith leaders, ANCs, and others to help defend our neighbors from warrantless attacks. Home Rule constraints can’t become an excuse for inaction or capitulation — and in a time of so much fear, elected leaders must stand ready to defend our communities from such attacks.

responses.topThreeActions:
Over the last almost four years, I am most proud of three actions I have taken in support of DC Statehood. First, I have consistently fought against congressional interference in our local laws, using my vote and my voice to defend the District’s autonomy whenever Congress attempted to override the will of DC residents. Protecting Home Rule is foundational to the broader fight for statehood.

Second, I have used my platform to actively educate leaders and audiences outside of DC about why statehood is a matter of civil rights, democracy, and racial equity. Whether in national forums, meetings with stakeholders, or public commentary, I have made clear that taxation without representation is unacceptable in 2026.

Third, I have publicly and unequivocally endorsed DC Statehood as a policy priority, integrating it into my advocacy rather than treating it as symbolic rhetoric. Statehood is not an abstract issue. It is about full voting representation, budget autonomy, and self-determination for our residents, and I will continue advancing that fight both inside and outside the District.
responses.intendedActions: I have and intend to hold the line aggressively against congressional interference, including in the current tax fight. When Congress attempts to overturn or undermine locally enacted revenue measures, I will use every available platform to defend the District’s authority to govern its own budget and tax policy.
responses.congressResponse:
When Congress has attempted to overturn DC laws or interfere with our budget, I have responded immediately and publicly. I have educated residents about what was at stake through town halls, media appearances, and direct communication, making clear how congressional interference harms DC families in real and tangible ways. I have worked with my Council colleagues to pass formal resolutions rejecting interference and affirming our commitment to Home Rule.

I have also lobbied members of Congress, met with federal offices, and partnered with national civil rights and democracy organizations to build opposition to these efforts. When necessary, I have supported exploring legal strategies through the Attorney General. I have refused to normalize interference as routine, and I will continue using my voice and my office to defend DC’s autonomy and advance Statehood.
responses.partners:
In promoting DC Statehood, I intend to continue working closely with our Delegate to Congress, our Shadow Representative and Shadow Senators, and the DC Democratic Party.

I have an active working relationship with our Delegate’s office and have partnered on messaging and advocacy when Congress has attempted to interfere with DC laws or our budget. I have also engaged with our Shadow delegation to amplify statehood education efforts and align local and national advocacy strategies. In addition, I have worked with leaders within the DC Democratic Party to elevate Statehood as a core civil rights and democracy issue in local and national political spaces. These relationships are ongoing and collaborative, and I will continue strengthening them to ensure our push for Statehood is coordinated, visible, and persistent.
responses.voterInvolvement:
I believe Statehood will only be won if DC residents are organized, informed, and mobilized. I have already worked to educate voters about congressional interference and what it means for our budget, our laws, and our rights. Most recently, I led a delegation of nearly 50 Ward 5 neighbors to Capitol Hill to meet directly with Members of Congress and their staff to lobby against harmful congressional action. That kind of direct civic engagement matters. It shows that DC residents are not passive observers. We are active participants in defending our democracy.

Going forward, I will continue hosting town halls, organizing advocacy days, and partnering with civic and community organizations to equip residents with the tools to contact Congress, submit testimony, and elevate their voices nationally. Statehood cannot just be a slogan from elected officials. It must be a people powered movement. My role is to educate, convene, and mobilize residents so they are empowered to demand full representation and self determination.
responses.additionalComments:
Now more than ever, DC needs serious, steady leadership in the face of unprecedented congressional interference and political uncertainty. Statehood is not a symbolic issue for me. It is about protecting our budget, our public safety laws, our healthcare programs, and our fundamental right to self governance. Given the level of change and disruption facing the District, we must rely on experienced, proven leaders who understand both the policy and political terrain and who believe deeply in Statehood as a matter of civil rights and democracy.

I have not wavered on this issue. I have fought against congressional overreach, educated audiences inside and outside the District, mobilized residents to advocate on the Hill, and used my platform to center Statehood in the broader national conversation. DC voters deserve representation that is consistent, informed, and unafraid to defend our autonomy. I remain fully committed to that fight.

responses.topThreeActions: I have been a consistent and fierce advocate for full DC Statehood over the years. I’ve met directly with numerous members of Congress and Democratic House leadership, I’ve walked side-by-side with DC residents advocating and educating members of Congress, and I’ve joined public rallies to declare clearly and loudly why DC Statehood is needed now more than ever. I’ve also defended Council-passed laws under threat from the Trump Administration and Congress.
responses.intendedActions: I have consistently and fiercely defended DC Statehood for years. I have worked to develop relationships with members of Congress to help educate them about the importance of DC Statehood and to be our champions. I will also continue to be active in resident actions at the Capitol and elsewhere to join grassroots movements fighting for DC Statehood. And when Home Rule or DC laws are threatened, I won’t stay silent or sit out the fight. As I have demonstrated, I will speak out and show up to declare clearly and loudly why DC Statehood is needed now more than ever.
responses.congressResponse: As a current elected official, I use my position to speak loudly against any and all congressional attempts to overturn DC laws and encourage residents to make their voices heard. I have defended the District’s laws and local control. Not every DC elected official has shown up when it mattered, but I have. Throughout the past 12 months, I’ve worked strategically to push the Council to bring on advocacy capacity, lobby members of Congress, partner with advocacy efforts like Free DC, and use the power of my office to speak in press, public appearances, and directly to my constituents about why action must be taken to defend the District of Columbia.

These actions cannot be done only when it’s easy or convenient, but elected officials must demonstrate the courage to show up and speak out every day and in every fight.

Whether it’s addressing a convention of out-of-town visitors or elected colleagues, or sitting down with our local Scouts or school children, educating and advocating for DC Statehood - and highlighting the inherent injustice that still exists today - must be part of every engagement strategy. It was even my legislation the Council passed to change DC’s license plates to read “End Taxation Without Representation” - to remind everyone that statehood and autonomy will only be won through action, strategy, and organizing.
